frames.gloss: 第N个要避免的误区是做某事（序数列举）
frames.notes: one后接不定式to avoid后置修饰

examples.text: The second one to avoid is focusing on negative goals.
The third one to avoid is using the same strategies in different circumstances.
The fourth one to avoid is not forgiving ourselves for slipping up.

frames.frame: [从句/主语], [人名] told me / found, [谓语]
frames.gloss: 双逗号插入报道来源，交代是谁说的
frames.notes: 插入语非主干，易误当主句

examples.text: While educators and parents have successfully convinced students of the need to be high performing and diligent, the experts told me, they haven’t adequately prepared them for the inevitability of failure.
One such society was the Zuni Indians of Arizona, and they, Mead found, valued cooperation far more than competition.

frames.gloss: 对A的反应或做法不同于对B
frames.notes: than后用do替代重复动词，勿误读主干

examples.text: Our brains respond to language expressing facts differently than they do to words conveying possibility, scientists at New York University have recently found.
We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work.

frames.frame: One theory is that [S V] / Another (theory) is that [S V]
frames.gloss: 一种理论认为…，另一种理论认为…（假设列举）
frames.notes: another后省略theory，科技文常见路标
frames.related: One of the [复数名词] of/about [X] is that [S V]

examples.text: One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not.
Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations.

frames.frame: [S] be found / have been shown to [V]
frames.gloss: 研究发现某人或某物具有某特征（无施动者）
frames.notes: 被动+不定式报道，研究者隐含

examples.text: Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals.
Bilingual individuals have been shown to have smaller vocabularies and to take longer in retrieving words from memory when compared to monolinguals.

frames.gloss: 把前句内容概括成一个名词，再用that从句展开评论
frames.notes: 回指同位语；名词是前句总结

examples.text: The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.

In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience — a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly.
Darwin’s theory has even been summarized as “survival of the fittest” — a phrase Darwin himself never used — further highlighting competition’s role in success.

frames.frame: [比较级] than [S] might think / might lead you to believe
frames.gloss: 比你以为的更…（暗示读者预期不准）
frames.notes: 比较级后接认知动词从句表反预期

examples.text: Bilingualism and multilingualism are actually more common than you might think.
Once again, however, the results are far less clear than the popular media might lead you to believe.

frames.gloss: 无论它是什么／无论X如何，主句照说
frames.notes: whatever后直接接名词＝省略is的让步

examples.text: Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life.
Whatever your reward, it has to be more than just the activity itself to get you going.

frames.frame: That's why [S V] / Which is why [S V]
frames.gloss: 这就是为什么；which回指前整句
frames.notes: Which is why可独立成句，口语笔调

examples.text: That’s why rather than giving up something, think with the behaviors you want to stop.
Which is why it’s so hard to maintain new behaviors.

frames.frame: There is (some) reason/evidence to believe (that) [S V]
frames.notes: 存在句引出依据，语气留有余地

examples.text: However, there is some reason to believe that learning languages might be different.
In fact, there is evidence to support this claim.

frames.gloss: 做某事有困难（如睡不好、想不起词）

examples.text: At any age, we might experience difficulty finding the exact word we want or have trouble remembering the name of the person we just met.
Classical music can also be a great tool to help people who have trouble sleeping.

frames.notes: whole other为口语化搭配，＝entirely different

examples.text: Once we’ve successfully made that change, we then have to make other adjustments to our lives to ensure that we continue to maintain it, which is often a whole other challenge in itself.
Research shows it is quite another challenge to maintain a behavioral change after you have initiated it.

candidates.frame: Just because [S V] doesn't mean [S V]

examples.text: Just because you might have temporarily strayed off course doesn’t mean you can’t start afresh the next day.

candidates.gloss: 绝非、一点也不（后接形容词）
candidates.related: nothing less than [X] / nothing short of [X]

examples.text: And here’s the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality. “In this era of choice, entertainment media are what captures hearts and minds,” Kim writes. “Its political consequences are anything but trivial”.

candidates.notes: fact that同位语从句作despite宾语

examples.text: Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty.

candidates.gloss: 在…之中，大多数…（部分-整体前置）
candidates.notes: of短语提前总揽再谈部分

examples.text: Of around 650 spider species regularly recorded in the UK, the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland.

candidates.frame: If [前提], then we would expect to see [推论]
candidates.gloss: 若假设成立，按理应观察到某结果

examples.text: If the benefits of being bilingual spill over to other aspects of cognition, then we would expect to see a lower incidence of Alzheimer’s disease in bilinguals than in monolinguals, or at least a later onset of Alzheimer’s for bilinguals.

candidates.frame: In an age where [S V], [主句]
candidates.gloss: 在一个…的时代（背景化开头）
candidates.notes: where引导时代名词的定语从句

examples.text: In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your you who define who you are.

candidates.frame: There is general consensus among [X] that [S V]
candidates.gloss: 在某群体中有普遍共识认为…

examples.text: There is general consensus among experts that willpower alone cannot guarantee one’s success in changing and maintaining a habit.

candidates.gloss: 比如说…（祈使词引入假设）

examples.text: Say your goal is to run five miles three times a week, and this week you ran one mile on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

candidates.gloss: 不是A而是B（强调句版先否后纠）

examples.text: Sometimes, it’s not your process that lets you down, but the habit that you want to change in the first place.

candidates.gloss: 一派是…（下句常接The opposing side…）
candidates.notes: 地点倒装引出争论一方

examples.text: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn’t worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy.
It is reasonable to conclude that spending is praiseworthy, supposing it is not beyond your means.

candidates.gloss: 问题在于…（后接直接疑问句）

examples.text: The question is: how badly do you really want to change?
